extracted.intended_audience: D.C. Bar members, other lawyers, law firms, corporate legal departments, and non-lawyers (potential commenters on proposed rule changes)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit written comments addressing the need for and the text of proposed amendments to the District of Columbia Rules of Professional Conduct concerning client-generated engagement letters and outside counsel guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict practices that limit prospective clients' choice of counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit certain practices that restrict the ability of prospective clients to engage counsel of their choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee's proposed amendments are intended to prevent client-generated terms that would effectively bar or deter a prospective client from selecting counsel they prefer. Commenters should address the need for limiting such practices and the text of any proposed rule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit practices that impose restrictions on lawyers' independence and right to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit practices that impose restrictions on lawyers’ independence and right to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed amendments target client-imposed conditions in engagement letters/OCGs that would impair a lawyer's independent professional judgment or ability to practice. Commenters may discuss scope and alternative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid provisions that render outside counsel liable for others' damages without fault
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit practices that can render outside counsel liable for damages sustained by clients or others through no fault of such counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle underlies a proposed amendment (see Rule 1.8 amendment) to prohibit lawyers from accepting conditions that expand liability beyond statute/common law. Commenters should evaluate whether the prohibition and its wording are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect lawyers' right to retain copies of client files (including work product)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit practices that restrict a lawyer’s right to retain a copy of a client’s file, including the lawyer’s work product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed amendment to Rule 1.16 would make clear a lawyer may retain copies of client files and work product, subject to confidentiality rules that may limit reuse. Commenters may address scope and limitations (e.g., confidentiality exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow use of general, non-client-specific knowledge for benefit of later clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit practices that restrict a lawyer’s right to make use of general, non-confidential information acquired in the course of a representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee proposes amending Rule 1.6 to make clear a lawyer is not only permitted but obligated to use general (i.e., not client-specific) knowledge gained earlier for subsequent clients. Commenters may discuss boundaries between general knowledge and confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit withdrawal when client unilaterally changes terms materially
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit practices that can compel outside counsel to accept clients’ unilateral changes in the terms of a representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed amendment to Rule 1.16 would provide that where a lawyer has agreed that the client may make unilateral changes, the lawyer may withdraw if the client makes a material change to which the lawyer is unwilling to assent. Commenters should assess what constitutes a 'material change' and appropriate standards for withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend Rules 1.7 and 5.6: remove open-ended permission to expand conflicts by agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend Rules 1.7 and 5.6 to remove the existing open-ended permission for a lawyer and client to expand the scope of what constitutes a conflict of interest under the D.C. Rules, except where broader coverage is required by other law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee seeks comment on eliminating client-lawyer agreements that broaden the definition of conflicts beyond the Rule, while preserving situations where other law requires broader coverage. Commenters are invited to propose less far-reaching approaches that would also appropriately limit the current open-ended ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend Rule 1.8: prohibit accepting conditions imposing broader liability than law
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend Rule 1.8 to prohibit a lawyer from proposing or accepting conditions that impose liability on a lawyer that is broader than the liability imposed by statute or common law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change targets client clauses that unilaterally expand counsel's liability. Commenters should address the need for the prohibition and the precise textual formulation to implement it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend Rule 1.16: clarify retention and reuse limits for client files/work product
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend Rule 1.16 to make clear that a lawyer may retain copies of client files, including the lawyer’s work product, but may not use that work product in other matters if the Rules’ confidentiality provisions prohibit such use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment separates the right to retain copies from the right to reuse work product; commenters may discuss how confidentiality rules should govern reuse and the practical effects on file retention practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend Rule 1.6: clarify obligation to use general knowledge for subsequent clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend Rule 1.6 to make clear that a lawyer is not only permitted, but obligated, to use general (i.e., not client-specific) knowledge gained in the course of a representation for the benefit of subsequent clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should consider boundaries between general knowledge and confidential client information, and whether an affirmative obligation is appropriate or how it should be expressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend Rule 1.16: allow withdrawal when client makes material unilateral changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend Rule 1.16 to provide that where a lawyer has agreed that her client may make unilateral changes in the terms of a representation, the lawyer may withdraw if the client makes a material change to which the lawyer is unwilling to assent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may propose criteria for 'material change,' procedural protections, notice periods, or other guardrails to balance client autonomy and lawyer rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment scope requirement: address both need and text of proposed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters should address the need for as well as the text of the proposed amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive feedback should include whether the changes are necessary, and suggested precise drafting or alternative language where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to consider alternative, less far-reaching approaches on conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters also are invited to address the proposed amendments regarding conflicts of interest, and specifically whether there are other, less far-reaching approaches that would appropriately limit the current open-ended ability of lawyers and clients to set the limits of what constitutes a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee is explicitly seeking alternatives to outright removal of the open-ended permission; commenters may offer narrower or tailored solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and deadline requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be in writing and submitted by email to [email protected] (Attn: Rules of Professional Conduct Review Committee) no later than COB February 11, 2021 (90 days after publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement — late or non-written submissions may not be considered. Include sufficient detail and proposed text as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity/identification assurance regarding published references to comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee’s intention is that any future publication referencing comments received in response to this request will not include details that would identify commenters, regardless of whether feedback is submitted in an individual capacity or on behalf of a group or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an assurance about how comments may be referenced in future publications; commenters should be aware that the Committee intends to anonymize identifying details.
